rows.speaker: منذر بن سعيد
rows.claim: Mundhir ibn Sa'id reports a reading with an initial alif, أفظن.
rows.anchor: وحكى القاضى منذر بن سعيد: أن بعضهم قرأ «أفظن» بالألف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the three darknesses as night, sea, and the whale.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة منهم ابن عباس وقتادة: ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الحوت

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jonah heard stones glorifying God at the earth's depths, called from three darknesses, and was cast ashore sick like a featherless chick.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن مسعود في بيت المال قال: لما ابتلع الحوت يونس عليه السلام أهوى به إلى قرار الأرض

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd says the darknesses were the sea and a whale that had swallowed the first whale.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة منهم سالم بن أبي الجعد: ظلمة البحر، وظلمة حوت التقم الحوت الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural can refer just to the first whale's interior: every side is dark, so using the plural is idiomatic, as in the well's dark recesses.
rows.anchor: ويصح أن يعبر بالظلمات عن جوف الحوت الأول فقط كما قال: «في غيابات الجب» وفي كل جهاته ظلمة فجمعها سائغ

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests the darknesses may be sin, distress, and loneliness.
rows.anchor: وذكر الماوردي: أنه يحتمل أن يعبر بالظلمات عن ظلمة الخطيئة، وظلمة الشدة، وظلمة الوحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God told the whale not to harm even one hair: its belly was Jonah's prison, not his food.
rows.anchor: وروي: أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى الحوت: «لا تؤذ منه شعرة فإني جعلت بطنك سجنه ولم أجعله طعامك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jonah prostrated inside the whale after hearing the fish glorify God in the sea's depths.
rows.anchor: وروي: أن يونس عليه السلام سجد في جوف الحوت حين سمع تسبيح الحيتان في قعر البحر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan reports that Jonah thought he had died, discovered he was alive, resumed his customary prayer, and called the whale's belly a mosque where none had prayed before.
rows.anchor: عن عوف عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن قال: لما التقم الحوت يونس عليه السلام ظن أنه قد مات فطول رجليه فإذا هو لم يمت

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي
rows.claim: Abu al-Ma'ali explains that the Prophet was no nearer to God at the Lote Tree than Jonah was in the whale at the sea's bottom; this shows God is not spatially located.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو المعالي: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا تفضلوني على يونس بن متى " المعنى فإني لم أكن وأنا في سدرة المنتهى بأقرب إلى الله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison of the Prophet with Jonah supports the conclusion that God is not in any direction.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الباري سبحانه وتعالى ليس في جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah called himself wrong for abandoning persistent care for his people and patience with them.
rows.anchor: يريد فيما خالف فيه من ترك مداومة قومه والصبر عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that Jonah counted his departure wrong because he left without permission.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في الخروج من غير أن يؤذن له

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says Jonah's ordeal was purification rather than punishment, since prophets cannot be punished; even children who do not deserve punishment may be disciplined.
rows.anchor: وقد يؤدب من لا يستحق العقاب كالصبيان ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Jonah meant his supplication against his people for punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الظالمين في دعائي على قومي بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah also prayed against his people without being taken to account, as Jonah was not for this confession.
rows.anchor: وقد دعا نوح على قومه فلم يؤاخذ

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Jonah declared God free of injustice and assigned wrongdoing to himself, as Adam and Eve did because they placed themselves outside their proper station.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي في معناه: نزه ربه عن الظلم وأضاف الظلم إلى نفسه اعترافا واستحقاقا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that the Prophet said no Muslim ever invokes God with Jonah's prayer in a matter without being answered.
rows.anchor: روى أبو داود عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " دعاء ذي النون في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say that Jonah's supplication contains God's greatest name.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إنه اسم الله الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report promises that God will answer the one who calls and save them as He saved Jonah; here the promise is implicit in Jonah's confession of wrongdoing rather than an explicit request.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية شرط الله لمن دعاه أن يجيبه كما أجابه وينجيه كما أنجاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God frees believers from their distress through their prior good works; Jonah's earlier worship was preserved as a divine honoring of his devotion and obedience.
rows.anchor: أي نخلصهم من همهم بما سبق من عملهم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq argues that since Jonah spent only a few days with the whale yet is forever called Dhun-Nun, God would not waste the devotion of a servant who worshipped for seventy years.
rows.anchor: صحب ذو النون الحوت أياما قلائل فإلى يوم القيامة يقال له ذو النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, “the grief” means the belly of the whale.
rows.anchor: الغم } أي من بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: The common reading has two nuns from anja; Ibn Amir reads one doubled nun as a past passive verb, with an understood verbal noun as subject and a quiescent yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر «نجي» بنون واحدة وجيم مشددة وتسكين الياء

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيد وثعلب
rows.claim: Al-Farra, Abu Ubayd, and Tha'lab accept Ibn Amir's reading by treating an omitted verbal noun as the passive subject; the yāʾ is quiescent by a dialect pattern also found in poetry and Qur'anic recitation.
rows.anchor: هذا تأويل الفراء وأبي عبيد وثعلب في تصويب هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم والزجاج
rows.claim: Abu Hatim and al-Zajjaj call the reading ungrammatical: it makes the object accusative under a passive verb, and the proposed construction is pointless and cannot be supported by poetry against the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وخطأها أبو حاتم والزجاج وقالوا: هو لحن لأنه نصب اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد والقتبي
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd and al-Qutaybi offer another explanation: the nūn assimilates into the jīm.
rows.anchor: ولأبي عبيد قول آخر وقاله القتبي وهو أنه أدغم النون في الجيم

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects assimilation because nūn and jīm have distant articulation points; “min jāʾa” likewise cannot become “mjāʾa.”
rows.anchor: النحاس: وهذا القول لا يجوز عند أحد من النحويين لبعد مخرج النون من مخرج الجيم

rows.speaker: علي بن سليمان
rows.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman explains the form as the regular ننجي with one of its two adjacent nūns deleted, like dropping one of the two tāʾs in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: الأصل ننجي فحذف إحدى النونين لاجتماعهما كما تحذف إحدى التاءين

rows.speaker: محمد بن السميقع وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa and Abu al-Aliya read “and thus Allah saved the believers” with an active verb and explicit divine subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميقع وأبو العالية «وكذلك نجى المومنين» أي نجى الله المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author judges the active reading of Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa and Abu al-Aliya to be good.
rows.anchor: أي نجى الله المؤمنين وهي حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabur and book are equivalent terms: zabara means “to write,” and zubur is its plural, so the Torah and Gospel may also be called zabur.
rows.anchor: الزبور والكتاب واحد ولذلك جاز أن يقال للتوراة والإنجيل زبور

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Zabur means the Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, while the Reminder is the heavenly record.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: «الزبور» التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi identifies the Zabur as David's Psalms and the Reminder as Moses' Torah.
rows.anchor: الشعبي: «الزبور» زبور داود، و«الذكر» توراة موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd say the Zabur means the prophets' books and the Reminder is the heavenly Mother of the Book.
rows.anchor: مجاهد وابن زيد: «الزبور» كتب الأنبياء عليهم السلام، و«الذكر» أم الكتاب الذي عند الله في السماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Zabur means books sent to prophets after Moses and the Reminder is the Torah revealed to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «الزبور» الكتب التي أنزلها الله من بعد موسى على أنبيائه

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads الزُّبُر with a ḍamma on zāy, using the plural form zubur.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «في الزبور» بضم الزاي جمع زبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best interpretation is that “the earth” is the earth of Paradise: worldly land has already been inherited by righteous and unrighteous alike; this is also attributed to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others.
rows.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه أنه يراد بها أرض الجنة كما قال سعيد بن جبير لأن الأرض في الدنيا قد ورثها الصالحون وغيرهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Mujahid and Abu al-Aliya cite the people of Paradise saying God fulfilled His promise and gave them the earth as evidence for the Paradise interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو العالية: ودليل هذا التأويل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the inherited land as the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أنها الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Muhammad's community inherits the lands of unbelieving nations through conquest.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: أنها أرض الأمم الكافرة ترثها أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفتوح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the righteous inheritors as the Children of Israel, citing their inheritance of the blessed land.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد بذلك بنو إسرائيل بدليل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the righteous servants as Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن المراد بالعباد الصالحين أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the yāʾ in عبادي as quiescent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «عبادي الصالحون» بتسكين الياء

words: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In this” refers to the admonition and reminders discussed in this sura; another explanation takes it to mean the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي فيما جرى ذكره في هذه السورة من الوعظ والتنبيه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وسفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra and Sufyan al-Thawri identify worshippers as those who perform the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة وسفيان الثوري: هم أهل الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses worshippers as obedient people; ʿābid also carries the sense of being humbled and submissive.
rows.anchor: مطيعين. والعابد المتذلل الخاضع

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says the phrase can include every rational person, since human nature entails humility before the Creator and contemplating and applying the Qur'an can guide one to Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: ولا يبعد أن يدخل فيه كل عاقل لأنه من حيث الفطرة متذلل للخالق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the worshippers as Muhammad's community, who pray five times daily and fast Ramadan; this is the same view as the first report.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: هم أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الذين يصلون الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” can be nominative, with an implied “your obligation is that,” or accusative, with an implied command to carry it out.
rows.anchor: بتقدير: فرضكم ذلك، أو الواجب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative is an eloquent pointing expression, comparable to the wording in Zuhayr's verse.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذه الإشارة البليغة قول زهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred matters first refer to pilgrimage rites mentioned in 22:29; veneration of sacred places is included, according to Ibn Zayd and others.
rows.anchor: والحرمات المقصودة هنا هي أفعال الحج المشار إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, the sacred matters mean obeying God's commands in obligatory duties and recommended practices.
rows.anchor: الحرمات امتثال الأمر في فرائضه وسننه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revering God's sacred matters benefits a person more than neglecting any of them.
rows.anchor: أي التعظيم خير له عند ربه من التهاون بشيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes “better” as a promise of good for the person, rather than a comparative.
rows.anchor: وليست للتفضيل وإنما هي عدة بخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock made lawful for eating are camels, cattle, and sheep.
rows.anchor: أن تأكلوها وهي الإبل والبقر والغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception refers to prohibited animals recited in scripture, including carrion, animals killed by blows, and related categories.
rows.anchor: أي في الكتاب من المحرمات وهي الميتة والموقوذة وأخواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock rule connects with pilgrimage, where sacrifice is offered, by clarifying which animals may be slaughtered and eaten.
rows.anchor: ولهذا اتصال بأمر الحج فإن في الحج الذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the exception excludes game while you are in a state of ihram.
rows.anchor: غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs means something filthy; a wathan is an image made of wood, iron, gold, silver, or similar material, which Arabs set up and worship.
rows.anchor: الرجس: الشيء القذر. والوثن: التمثال من خشب أو حديد أو ذهب أو فضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Christian cross is like an idol because Christians erect, worship, and venerate it.
rows.anchor: والنصارى تنصب الصليب وتعبده وتعظمه فهو كالتمثال أيضا

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: Adi ibn Hatim reports that when he came to the Prophet wearing a gold cross, the Prophet told him to remove that idol, meaning the cross.
rows.anchor: وقال عدي بن حاتم: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي عنقي صليب من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word wathan derives from something standing in its place; an idol is named for being fixed upright in one place and not moving away.
rows.anchor: وأصله من وثن الشيء أي أقام في مقامه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj explain the command as avoiding the worship of idols.
rows.anchor: يريد اجتنبوا عبادة الأوثان روي عن ابن عباس وابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols are called filth because they cause divine punishment.
rows.anchor: وسماها رجسا لأنها سبب الرجز وهو العذاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view calls idols impure; impurity is a legal status rather than an intrinsic property of objects, and is removed only through faith, just as ritual purification requires water.
rows.anchor: وليست النجاسة وصفا ذاتيا للأعيان وإنما هي وصف شرعي من أحكام الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min may explain the kind of filth, restricting this prohibition to idol filth while other filth is forbidden elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنها لبيان الجنس، فيقع نهيه عن رجس الأوثان فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min marks the starting point: a general ban on filth begins with idol worship, which gathers every corruption and filth.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون لابتداء الغاية فكأنهم نهاهم عن الرجس عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking min as partitive reverses and corrupts the verse's meaning.
rows.anchor: ومن قال إن «من» للتبعيض، قلب معنى الآية وأفسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zūr means falsehood and lies; it is so named because it deviates from truth, as in the cave verse's “turning aside” and the name of a slanted city; anything other than truth is falsehood.
rows.anchor: والزور: الباطل والكذب. وسمي زورا لأنه أميل عن الحق

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said in a sermon that false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: عدلت شهادة الزور الشرك بالله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports from Anas that when God created the Garden of Eden and planted its trees by His hand, He told it to speak and it said, “Successful are the believers.”
rows.anchor: روى البيهقي من حديث أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet prayed facing the Kaaba, began this sura, then coughed and bowed when Moses or Jesus was mentioned; Muslim reports it similarly.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي عن عبد الله بن السائب قال: حضرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الفتح فصلى في قبل الكعبة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Umar that revelation sounded like bees near the Prophet; afterward the Prophet prayed for increase, acceptance, and contentment, then said ten verses had been revealed whose observance admits one to Paradise, and recited them; Ibn al-Arabi authenticated the report.
rows.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas glosses “whoever upholds them” as adhering to the ten verses without violating their teachings, like someone carrying out his work.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: معنى «من أقامهن» من أقام عليهن ولم يخالف ما فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligations of ablution and pilgrimage were revealed after these ten verses and were included among what believers must uphold.
rows.anchor: ثم نزل بعد هذه الآيات فرض الوضوء والحج فدخل معهن

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads the hamza with ḍamma as a passive verb, meaning the believers were made successful or preserved in reward and good.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «قد أفلح المؤمنون» بضم الألف على الفعل المجهول

rows.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet used to look toward the sky during prayer; after this verse was revealed, he directed his gaze to the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: روى المعتمر عن خالد عن محمد بن سيرين قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ينظر إلى السماء في الصلاة

rows.speaker: هشيم
rows.claim: In Hushaym's version, Muslims used to look around during prayer; after the verses were revealed, they faced the prayer and looked ahead.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية هشيم: كان المسلمون يلتفتون في الصلاة وينظرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers readers to his discussion in al-Baqara of the ruling on praying toward the direction one looks.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم ما للعلماء في حكم المصلي إلى حيث ينظر في «البقرة» عند قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier discussions of khushuʿ's meaning in al-Baqara, including its locus in the heart and the limbs' following the heart as their ruler.
rows.anchor: والخشوع محله القلب فإذا خشع خشعت الجوارح كلها لخشوعه إذ هو ملكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A learned man would fear God when standing for prayer, avoiding both wandering his eyes and thinking about worldly matters.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل من العلماء إذا أقام الصلاة وقام إليها يهاب الرحمن

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata defines humility in prayer as not fiddling with any part of one's body.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: هو ألا يعبث بشيء من جسده في الصلاة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet saw a man playing with his beard during prayer and said that if his heart were humble, his limbs would be humble too.
rows.anchor: وأبصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يعبث بلحيته في الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet said that mercy faces a person who stands to pray, so they should not move pebbles; al-Tirmidhi transmits it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ذر قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem praises prayer as comprehensive good, in which the limbs submit to God, mercy meets the worshipper, and the worshipper becomes intimate with the Lord if humble.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ألا في الصلاة الخير والفضل أجمع

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni reports that when Aisha was asked about the Prophet's character, she had the people recite this sura through “they carefully maintain,” pointing to the verses as a description of him.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو عمران الجوني قال: قيل لعائشة ما كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet glanced right and left in prayer but did not turn his neck behind him.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يلحظ في صلاته يمينا وشمالا

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik says that while he prayed near the Prophet he sometimes glanced at him; the Prophet returned the look, then looked away when Ka'b turned toward him, and did not order him to repeat the prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب بن مالك في حديثه الطويل: ثم أصلي قريبا منه يعني من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether khushuʿ is a prayer obligation or a virtue completing it; the author says the correct view is that it is obligatory and located in the heart.
rows.anchor: على قولين. والصحيح الأول، ومحله القلب

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit says khushuʿ is the first knowledge to be taken from people; al-Tirmidhi calls the report through Jubayr ibn Nufayr hasan gharīb, and al-Nasa'i also transmits it through Awf ibn Malik with a sound chain.
rows.anchor: وهو أول علم يرفع من الناس قاله عبادة بن الصامت

rows.speaker: معاوية بن صالح
rows.claim: Mu'awiya ibn Salih was judged reliable by Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, Ahmad, and Abu Zur'a and used by Muslim; Abu Hatim considered him acceptable for recording but not proof, Yahya ibn Ma'in differed, and only Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan is said to have criticized him.
rows.anchor: قلت: معاوية بن صالح أبو عمرو ويقال أبو عمر الحضرمي الحمصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the meanings of idle talk and zakat were already discussed in al-Baqara and need not be repeated.
rows.anchor: وتقدم في «البقرة» معنى اللغو والزكاة فلا معنى للإعادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the condemned idle talk here is associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إن اللغو هنا الشرك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says idle talk here means all sins, a broad view that encompasses the narrower explanations of shirk and singing.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: إنه المعاصي كلها

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik ibn Anas transmits from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir the view that idle talk means singing; fuller discussion is deferred to Luqman.
rows.anchor: كما روى مالك بن أنس عن محمد بن المنكدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāʿilūn means those who perform or pay it; this usage is eloquent and attested in Arab speech, including poetry by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «فاعلون» أي مؤدون وهي فصيحة، وقد جاءت في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad and other jurists of the school say temporary marriage was first allowed, prohibited by the Prophet at Khaybar, allowed again at the conquest, and prohibited afterward; Ibn al-Arabi alluded to this account.
rows.anchor: كانت مباحة ثم حرمها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زمن خيبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking sexual relations outside the permitted wives and owned bondwomen is transgression; the author says this warrants the prescribed penalty, including for sodomy, as scripture calls its practitioners transgressors.
rows.anchor: من نكح ما لا يحل عاديا، وأوجب عليه الحد لعدوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author qualifies the penalty ruling: it requires consideration when a person is ignorant or interpreting the law, which can prevent the penalty despite the reported consensus that the cited exception applies only to men.
rows.anchor: قلت: فيه نظر، ما لم يكن جاهلا أو متأولا، وإن كان الإجماع منعقدا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that a woman who had sex with her male slave claimed she thought ownership made him lawful as it did a woman for a man; Umar consulted the Companions, who ruled she had misinterpreted scripture and could not be stoned, though Umar barred her from marrying again and ordered the slave kept away.
rows.anchor: روى معمر عن قتادة قال: تسررت امرأة غلامها فذكر ذلك لعمر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah reports that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz spared a married woman who had taken her handsome slave as a concubine because she was ignorant, but ordered the slave sold and removed from her region.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر بن عبد الله أنه سمع أباه يقول: أنا حضرت عمر بن عبد العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waraʾ means “apart from” or “beyond”; here it is the object of seeking, meaning seeking beyond one's wives and owned bondwomen.
rows.anchor: و«وراء» بمعنى سوى، وهو مفعول ب«ابتغى»

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead treats the object of seeking as omitted and waraʾ as an adverb meaning what lies beyond that.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أي فمن ابتغى ما بعد ذلك فمفعول الابتغاء محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative dhalik can point to everything previously mentioned, whether feminine or masculine.
rows.anchor: و«ذلك» يشار به إلى كل مذكور مؤنثا كان أو مذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿādūn are those who cross the limit, from the verb ʿadā meaning to go beyond it.
rows.anchor: أي المجاوزون الحد من عدا أي جاوز الحد وجازه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Most readers have the plural amānāt, while Ibn Kathir reads the singular amānah.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «لأماناتهم» بالجمع. وابن كثير بالإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusts and covenants include everything a person undertakes in religious and worldly matters, by word, deed, or belief; they cover dealings and promises, require faithful preservation and fulfillment, and trust is broader than covenant.
rows.anchor: والأمانة والعهد يجمع كل ما يحمله الإنسان من أمر دينه ودنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new generation was brought into being after the destruction of Noah's people.
rows.anchor: أي من بعد هلاك قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the later generation as the people of Ad and its messenger as Hud, since no nation arose immediately after Noah except Ad.
rows.anchor: لأنه ما كانت أمة أنشئت في إثر قوم نوح إلا عاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as Thamud and their messenger as Salih, citing their destruction by a cry like the one mentioned in Hud.
rows.anchor: يعني صالحا. قالوا: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى آخر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that the people of Midian, Shuaib's people, were also seized by the cry and therefore could be intended.
rows.anchor: وممن أخذ بالصيحة أيضا أصحاب مدين قوم شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger was from their own clan, so they knew his birth and upbringing and would be more receptive to him.
rows.anchor: أي من عشيرتهم، يعرفون مولده ومنشأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ means the community's nobles, leaders, and chiefs.
rows.anchor: الملأ } أي الأشراف والقادة والرؤساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying the meeting with the Hereafter means denying resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: الذين كفروا وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's granting them worldly abundance made them insolent; atrafnāhum comes from tarfa, luxury like a fine gift.
rows.anchor: أي وسعنا عليهم نعم الدنيا حتى بطروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs argue that the messenger has no advantage over them because he needs the same food and drink.
rows.anchor: فلا فضل له عليكم لأنه محتاج إلى الطعام والشراب كأنتم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says an omitted min is understood: “he drinks from what you drink from.”
rows.anchor: على حذف من، أي مما تشربون منه

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians reject the need to omit min: if mā is a verbal noun it needs no resumptive pronoun; if relative, the object is simply omitted.
rows.anchor: ولا يحتاج إلى حذف ألبتة لأن «ما» إذا كان مصدرا لم يحتج إلى عائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean that those who obey the messenger will be cheated by abandoning their gods and following a man with no special merit over them.
rows.anchor: يريد لمغبونون بترككم آلهتكم واتباعكم إياه من غير فضيلة له عليكم

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَنَّكُم مُّخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise they deride is that after death and becoming dust and bones they will be raised from their graves.
rows.anchor: أي مبعوثون من قبوركم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats the first anna as the object of yaʿidukum and the second anna as its بدل.
rows.anchor: والثانية بدل منها هذا مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites Abdullah's reading without the first anna, comparing its syntax to “I think, if you leave, that you will regret it.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وفي قراءة عبد الله «أيعدكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون»

rows.speaker: الفراء والجرمي وأبو العباس المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Farra, al-Jurmi, and al-Mubarrad treat the second anna as a repetition for emphasis, made fitting by the sentence's length.
rows.anchor: إلى أن الثانية مكررة للتوكيد، لما طال الكلام

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash understands “your being raised” as an event that will occur; the second anna is nominative under an implicit verb, like saying “today, the battle.”
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: المعنى أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما يحدث إخراجكم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq allows reading both particles with kasra, since yaʿidukum can mean “does he say to you.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: ويجوز «أيعدكم إنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما إنكم مخرجون»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hi refers to this worldly life: they claim there is no life beyond the present one, denying an afterlife after resurrection.
rows.anchor: «هي» كناية عن الدنيا أي ما الحياة إلا ما نحن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to how they say “we die and live” while denying resurrection is that people begin as lifeless drops of semen and then live in this world.
rows.anchor: نكون مواتا، أي نطفا ثم نحيا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer takes the order as reversed: “we live and die,” as in the paired commands in Ali Imran.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فيه تقديم وتأخير أي إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that the ancestors die and their descendants live.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «نموت» يعني الآباء، «ونحيا» يعني الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny being raised after death.
rows.anchor: أي بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He” refers to the messenger, whom they accuse of inventing a lie against God.
rows.anchor: يعنون الرسول. إلا رجل { افترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means “before long”; mā is an added emphatic particle.
rows.anchor: أي عن قليل، و«ما» زائدة مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will surely become regretful for their disbelief; the lām is the lām of oath.
rows.anchor: على كفرهم، واللام لام القسم أي والله ليصبحن

rows.speaker: التفاسير
rows.claim: Commentaries say Gabriel cried out at them once, together with the wind God used to destroy them, and they all died.
rows.anchor: في التفاسير: صاح بهم جبريل عليه السلام صيحة واحدة مع الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ means dead and motionless, like flood debris of rotted and crumbled grasses and reeds.
rows.anchor: أي هلكى هامدين كغثاء السيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan means destruction; another explanation is that they were distanced from God's mercy.
rows.anchor: أي هلاكا لهم. وقيل بعدا لهم من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan is accusative as a verbal noun, like “watering” and “tending.”
rows.anchor: وهو منصوب على المصدر. ومثله سقيا له ورعيا
